repo: Closed-source, binary-only. No public repo: https://github.com/sourcegraph/amp returns GitHub's 404 page, and https://github.com/sourcegraph/amp-cli 404s. Distributed as npm `@ampcode/cli` + per-platform `@ampcode/cli-<os>-<arch>` (legacy alias `@sourcegraph/amp`), plus a native installer. Primary source analysed: https://registry.npmjs.org/@ampcode/cli-win32-x64/-/cli-win32-x64-0.0.1792540877-gcc084c.tgz (amp.exe, 104,442,192 bytes, Rust + embedded Bun JS bundle).
surfaces: CLI TUI (`amp`), execute mode (`amp -x`/`--execute`), machine output (`amp --execute --stream-json`), headless runner (`amp --no-tui`) + background daemon, IDE bridge (local socket `<data>\ide`, JetBrains plugin, `get_diagnostics` tool), and cloud surfaces (ampcode.com web app, macOS/iOS apps, Amp Cloud "orbs"). KEY ARCHITECTURAL FACT: the local CLI is a thin WebSocket client. The agent loop, tool decisions, transcript and model routing live server-side in Rivet actors (`/api/thread-actors`, `/api/threads/...`, namespace "transcript" in the Rivet KV backend). The CLI binary's own debug text says: "Start with the CLI log, actor logs, and Rivet DB/inspector as sources of truth ... for staging/prod, logs are in gcloud." There is no local message store, no local SQLite, no protobuf, no encryption.
binaries: Windows: `amp.exe` (win32-x64 npm `@ampcode/cli-win32-x64`; also `amp.bat` shim, npm `bin/amp.exe` → node `cli-wrapper.cjs` → native binary). POSIX: `amp` (darwin/linux, arm64+x64). Also `amp --no-tui` (runner/headless daemon) and `amp -x` (execute). The npm package is a stub: `@ampcode/cli` has 6 files (install.cjs, cli-wrapper.cjs, bin/amp.exe shim) that hardlink the platform binary. 4,505 published versions (0.0.1792540877-gcc084c analysed) — churn rate is extreme.

paths: WINDOWS PER-THREAD ACTIVITY LOG (the only candidate): %LOCALAPPDATA%\amp\logs\threads\<threadId>.log

Amp DATA dir: %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\amp  (NOT %APPDATA%) — contains session.json, last-threads\<hash>-<interactive|execute>-session.json, device-id.json, accounts\ (secrets), net\, runner\, daemon\, ide\, oauth\locks\
CONFIG dir: %USERPROFILE%\.config\amp\settings.json (+ skills\, plugins\) — confirmed by official docs
Amp writes diagnostics ABOUT Claude Code (not about itself): %USERPROFILE%\.amp\claude-diagnostics\<threadId>\sessions\<sessionId>.json
NOT a log: ~/.local/share/amp/last-threads/* — JSON state (agentMode, lastThreadId, externalAgentModel, launchCount). Workspace path is stored only as a HASH; there is no plaintext cwd anywhere.
storage.format: JSON Lines. The per-thread log uses LogTape's JSON formatter with `properties:"flatten"`, producing one flat JSON object per line: {"@timestamp":"<ISO-8601>","level":"INFO|DEBUG|WARN|ERROR","message":"<fixed diagnostic string>","logger":"<category>","threadId":"T-...","<other redacted props>":...}. The agent's real transcript is NOT stored locally (server-side Rivet KV, namespace "transcript"). No SQLite/protobuf/encrypted blob for thread data; the only `bun:sqlite` in the binary is Bun runtime + unrelated tool code (no `new Database(` call, no ".db" path).
storage.append_semantics: APPEND-ONLY and LIVE. The thread sink does `fs.createWriteStream(join(logs,'threads',threadId+'.log'), {flags:'a'})` and `stream.write(formatter(record))` per record — no rotation, no rewrite, no commit-at-end. Records are emitted at log level >= info (default; `--log-level` can change it) and only for records whose `properties.threadId` is a non-empty string. A per-thread cleanup pass deletes `*.log` files older than 7 days (604800000 ms). The `cli.log` file sink DOES rotate (maxSize 10 MB, maxFiles 2). Because the log lives under %LOCALAPPDATA% it is a CACHE location and can be evicted by Windows cleanup.
storage.session_file_naming: <threadId>.log inside %LOCALAPPDATA%\amp\logs\threads\  — threadId is the server thread id (docs show the `T-<uuid>` form, e.g. T-f9941a55-3765-421e-972f-05dc1138c3a3; exact on-disk prefix UNVERIFIED because I did not read any local Amp data, per instruction). Path is user-facing: the TUI has a "Copy log path to clipboard" command bound to the same join(logs,'threads',threadId+'.log').

fields.project: NOT RECOVERABLE. Zero log record contains cwd / workspaceRoot (exhaustive scan of all .info/.debug/.warn/.error call sites in the bundle found only one `cwd` key, in an npm-update helper, and two `workspaceRoot` keys in git-branch refresh). The only local cwd-ish value is a SHA hash inside the last-threads filename.
fields.model: NOT RECOVERABLE. Zero log record contains a model id (exhaustive scan: 0 hits for a `model:` key in any log call). Model routing (`CLAUDE_*`, `GPT_5_*`, `GEMINI_*`, `DEEPSEEK_V4_*`, `MINIMAX_M3`, ...) is a server-side enum; the local session.json only stores `externalAgentModel` for the legacy "external agent" mode.
fields.file_basename: NOT RECOVERABLE. The CLI's redaction layer explicitly strips tool inputs: the `tool_lease` summary keeps only `toolName`; `message_added`/`message_updated` keeps only role/blockCount/blockTypes/blockStates/messageState/hasUsage; `tool_progress` keeps only progressType/progressState/progressBlockCount/progressBlockTypes; filesystem messages keep only ok/entryCount/errorCode. The path helper `path:${e.path}` is used for in-flight request de-duplication, never for logging.
fields.tool_activity: PARTIAL — tool NAME only. The `tool_lease` server message yields `toolName` (e.g. Read, edit_file, create_file, apply_patch, Bash, shell_command, Grep, glob, web_search, read_web_page, oracle, Task, todo_write, undo_edit, skill, find_thread) and is logged as a "websocket message" record carrying threadId, toolName, toolCallId, parentToolCallId, direction, clientID. No arguments, no file path, no result.
fields.phase: PARTIAL. Derivable from record types: `tool_lease` => RunningTools; `delta` with role=assistant/state=generating => Thinking; `agent_state` records carry `agentMode` and `state` (e.g. fast/plaid) => could drive a sub-agent label. `compaction_started`/`compaction_complete` mark phase boundaries.
fields.timestamps: YES. `@timestamp` is ISO-8601 with milliseconds and Z suffix (new Date(a.timestamp).toISOString()) on every record. The first record of a thread file is a usable task-start proxy. `duration_ms`/`num_turns` exist only in the `--stream-json` `result` message, not in the local log.

parser_strategy: Do not reuse the Codex/Claude parsers. Add a dedicated `parse_amp_line` in src/events.rs that (1) json-parses the line, (2) requires the object to carry a string `threadId` (so we only consume per-thread records), (3) reads ONLY the fixed key set @timestamp/level/message/type/toolName/toolCallId/parentToolCallId/role/state/agentMode/progressType/progressState. Map: first record seen for a thread id => ParsedEvent::TaskStarted{started_at_ms} from @timestamp (ms epoch); type=="tool_lease" with a non-empty toolName => ParsedEvent::TrackedToolStarted{call_id: toolCallId, activity: ToolActivity{label: classify_tool(toolName.to_ascii_lowercase(), ""), file: None, language: None}}; type=="tool_progress" with progressState=="completed"/"done" => ParsedEvent::TrackedToolFinished{call_id: toolCallId} (only if a call_id is present; the log's tool_progress records carry progressType/progressState but often NOT toolCallId, so pair the finish with the most recent open tool lease for that thread id); type=="delta" with role=="assistant" => ParsedEvent::Thinking{reasoning: None}; type=="agent_state" => ParsedEvent::AgentDetected{agent: agentMode} (e.g. "fast"/"plaid"); parentToolCallId non-null on a tool_lease => ParsedEvent::SubagentSpawned{conversation_id: parentToolCallId, agent: toolName}. NEVER read message/result/content/text/properties fields other than the allowlist. NEVER fabricate a file name: file is always None, language always None. Amplitude: classify_tool already maps most Amp tool names correctly (read_file/Read -> "Reading project files"; edit_file/apply_patch -> "Editing files"; Bash/shell_command -> "Running command"; Grep/glob -> "Searching project"; web_search/read_web_page -> "Browsing documentation"; Task -> "Running coding agent"; todo_write -> "Planning changes"), but "create_file", "oracle", "skill", "find_thread" currently fall through to the "Using development tools" default — add "create_file" => "Creating files" and "oracle" => "Consulting model" to classify_tool, or accept the default.

PROVIDER VARIANT: `Provider::Amp` in src/provider.rs, display_name() => "Amp", has_session_tracking() => true only if the session-log path is implemented; otherwise false and rely on the focused-app path. from_executable(): add "amp" => Some(Self::Amp) — but note the collision risk: the AmpPlayer (Winamp fork) binary is also `amp.exe`, so gate on the window title or accept the small false-positive risk. from_window(): match a title containing "amp" + a thread/project hint; do not match a bare "amp" substring. default_activity() => "Working with coding agent" (same bucket as Codex/OpenCode/Aider).

SESSION SOURCE ROOT (not under home_dir() on all machines, so use dirs::data_local_dir() with a home fallback): `dirs::data_local_dir()` (== %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows) `.join("amp").join("logs").join("threads")`, fallback `home.join("AppData").join("Local").join("amp").join("logs").join("threads")`. Do NOT use %APPDATA%\amp — Amp does not use Roaming for logs. Note dirs 7.0.0 is already a dependency, so `data_local_dir()` needs no new crate. The Amp DATA dir `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\amp` is state-only (session.json, device-id.json, accounts/, net/, runner/, daemon/) and should NOT be added as a session source.

is_session_log RULE: filename ends with ".log" (case-insensitive) AND the stem matches `^[Tt]-[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F-]{20,}$` (thread ids are `T-<uuid>` per the docs). Must reject "cli.log", "headless.log", "no-tui.log" and anything not starting with a thread id — otherwise the parser would ingest the CLI-wide log, which mixes all threads into one file. Because the current implementation gates every provider on `.jsonl`, this needs a per-provider branch (like the existing DeepSeekHarness branch) rather than a shared suffix check. recent_logs(): the existing walker is fine — "amp", "logs" and "threads" are not dot-dirs and not in the skip list; but note the depth-5 walk is unnecessary if the root points straight at `logs\threads`.

WHAT MUST CHANGE IN watcher.rs / main.rs: for the native per-thread log, almost nothing — it is append-only newline-delimited JSON, so the existing LogTailer works as-is. Three things are still needed: (1) the is_session_log extension branch above; (2) per-thread correlation — the log file name IS the thread id, so ActivityState must key the session by file path / thread id, and TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished call ids must be namespaced per thread so two threads' identical toolu ids cannot cross; (3) TaskStarted synthesis, because unlike Codex/DSH there is no "session started" record — the first observed record of a thread file must seed started_at_ms. Also: the log is in a CACHE directory, so the worker must tolerate the file disappearing (rotation / Windows cleanup) — treat a vanished thread log as "session ended" rather than an error. NO SQLite crate, NO zstd, NO JSON-per-file handling, NO rewrite-detection is required for the native log.

THE RICH PATH (recommended, opt-in): Amp's CLI already emits a complete, documented, machine-readable JSONL stream of the whole conversation to stdout: `amp --execute --stream-json` (schema in https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/streaming-json). It contains an `init` system message with `cwd` and `session_id` (=> project + model-less session start), assistant `tool_use` blocks with `input` (e.g. `{"path":"/Users/orb/project"}` => file basename), user `tool_result` blocks (=> tool finished), and a final `result` message with `duration_ms`/`num_turns` (=> timer/completion). It is intentionally Claude-Code-compatible. A user can persist it with `amp --execute --stream-json >> %USERPROFILE%\.discodex\amp\stream.jsonl` (or a per-thread file). Discodex could add a second, explicitly user-configured Amp root (e.g. a `DISCODEX_AMP_STREAM_DIR` env var or a `~/.discodex/amp/` folder) whose files are parsed with the SAME Claude-Code-style parser, giving project + file + tool + phase + timer. That is the only route to the Codex/DSH richness level, and it requires the user to opt in; it is not harness-native.

FORMAT-CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE: very high. Upstream states plainly "No backward compatibility, no legacy features"; the npm package has 4,505 published versions, and the log schema is a free-form diagnostic log whose record set is chosen by internal debug code (not a published contract). Mitigations: (a) treat the Amp adapter as BEST-EFFORT — if a record has no recognised `type`, ignore it silently; never error out; (b) never let an unparseable Amp line clear an existing activity (fail to the previous state, not to idle); (c) whitelist the exact keys read, and ignore every other key, so a future upstream change that adds content fields cannot leak them to Discord; (d) cap the label set to classify_tool's fixed strings; (e) if the thread log stops appearing for a thread, expire the session rather than reporting a stale file; (f) treat the whole adapter as optional — the Discord presence must still work when the Amp log is absent (which is the common case for cloud "orb" threads, where no local executor exists at all and no local thread log is produced).

risks: The local per-thread log is a DIAGNOSTIC log, not a published event schema. Upstream explicitly ships no backward compatibility; the record set is whatever internal debug code happens to emit. High churn risk (4,505 npm versions). Fail safe = ignore unknown records, never clear state on a parse error.

It lives under %LOCALAPPDATA% (a CACHE root) and is deleted after 7 days; Windows Storage Sense / Disk Cleanup can delete it at any time, mid-session. The adapter must tolerate the file vanishing without erroring.
Log verbosity is user-controllable via --log-level; at a level below info there is NO thread log content at all, and Discodex would silently degrade to no activity.
Cloud "orb" threads and remote runners produce NO local executor and therefore NO local tool_lease records — the adapter covers only local CLI sessions.

Tool activity is name-only. There is no file basename, no cwd and no model, so the presence can never reach Codex/DSH richness. The Discord presence for Amp will show "Editing files" / "Searching project" etc. with NO project name, NO file and NO model.

Tool names in the log are the wire names (edit_file, shell_command, oracle, Task); several do not match the names the model sees and two ("create_file", "oracle") fall through classify_tool's default. Mapping must be allowlisted, not free-form.

LogTape's `properties:"flatten"` merges properties into the record root, so a future upstream change that starts putting a path or text into a property would silently land in the record. Mitigation: read a strict key allowlist and ignore everything else — never spread the whole object.
exe name collision: "amp.exe" is also the AmpPlayer (Winamp fork) binary. Gate from_executable("amp") on the window title or accept a rare false positive.
Logo trap: LobeHub's dark/amp*.png is the AMP Project, not Sourcegraph Amp. Using it would put the wrong product's icon in Discord.

Medium on the exact per-thread record set (the redaction helpers are deterministic, but I could not open a real thread log on this machine, per the instruction not to read local harness data, and the log level is user-configurable). Low/none on the "T-" filename prefix, which I could not verify against a real file.
summary: Sourcegraph Amp CLI is a server-backed agent, not a local-log harness. The local `amp` process is a thin WebSocket client; the agent loop, tool decisions, model routing and the full transcript live server-side in Rivet actors (`/api/thread-actors`, `/api/threads/...`, KV namespace "transcript"). Verified local paths on Windows: data dir %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\amp (state only — session.json, device-id.json, accounts/, net/, runner/, daemon/; the workspace path is stored only as a SHA hash), config %USERPROFILE%\.config\amp\settings.json (docs-confirmed), and the only activity-ish artifact %LOCALAPPDATA%\amp\logs\threads\<threadId>.log — NOT %APPDATA%\amp. That thread log is append-only, live, flat JSON Lines (LogTape JSON formatter, properties flattened), but it is a redacted DIAGNOSTIC log: its records carry only threadId, toolCallId, toolName, role, blockTypes/states, agentMode and an ISO-8601 @timestamp. An exhaustive scan of every .info/.debug/.warn/.error call site in the shipped binary shows ZERO occurrences of cwd, model, tool arguments, file paths, assistant text or tool output. Therefore project, current file basename and model are unrecoverable; only normalized tool activity (name), a rough phase and a timer proxy are. The one route to Codex/DSH-level richness is Amp's own documented `amp --execute --stream-json` stream (init.cwd, tool_use.input.path, result.duration_ms), which a user can redirect to a file — an opt-in, user-instrumented path, not a harness-native log. No SQLite/protobuf/encrypted store is involved, so no new Rust dependency is needed.
